# VAST G1-J8 (websynth)

> A browser-based virtual-analog synthesizer studio: 8-voice poly synth with a
> ladder filter, a 4-track 16-step note sequencer, an 8-track drum machine, an
> 8-slot sampler, a parameter-automation (motion) sequencer, per-bar arrangement
> chains, selectable time signatures with per-machine polyrhythm, live DJ FX,
> and WAV/MP3 audio export.
> Runs entirely client-side (vanilla TypeScript + Web Audio, no backend).

AI agents can author songs for this synth as a single JSON file, which the
user imports via Song panel -> Import (or opens via a share link).

## MCP server (tools, not just documents)

If you support MCP connectors, everything below is also available as TOOLS at:

    https://vast.status201.com/mcp     (Streamable HTTP, no authentication)

Eight read-only tools: get_params, get_song_format, validate_song, expand_song,
make_share_link, get_preset_format, validate_preset, expand_preset. Validating a
draft against the live registry beats guessing from a document — an unknown
parameter id or an out-of-range value comes back as a field-level error you can
fix, and make_share_link returns a URL that opens the finished song in the synth.

It speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over POST only; GET answers 405, so this is not a page to
fetch. Add it as a connector, or:

    claude mcp add --transport http websynth https://vast.status201.com/mcp

The rest of this file is the same material as documents, for agents without MCP.

## Song formats

Two JSON formats are accepted on import:

- `websynth-song-author` (v1) — the compact AUTHORING dialect, recommended for
  AI output (~40-80 lines). Melody banks are positional note lists ("A2",
  "C#4", null = rest, C4 = 60), drums/sampler are hit lists keyed by track
  name (kick, snare, chat, ohat, ltom, mtom, htom, clap / s1..s8), and song
  structure is a chain string like "AABA". Input-only: the app expands it to
  the canonical format on import.
  Schema: /schema/websynth-song-author.schema.json
- `websynth-song` (v7) — the canonical full format the app exports. Requires
  literal grids: seqBanks[4][16], drumBanks[4][8][16], optional
  samplerBanks[4][8][16] and motionBanks[4][16] (XY param automation).
  Older versions still load: every addition is optional. v7 adds seqTranspose
  (a semitone offset per seqChain slot), v6 seqTracks (note-sequencer tracks
  2-4) and v5 motionTracks (motion's two extra single-parameter tracks).
  Schema: /schema/websynth-song.schema.json

Dimensions: 4 banks (A/B/C/D) per machine; 16 sixteenth-note step CELLS per
bank (always exactly 16, whatever the meter — see below);
4 note-sequencer tracks per bank (track 1 in seqBanks, tracks 2-4 in the
optional seqTracks[bank][track], which is indexed by the real track number so
index 0 is always null); 8 drum tracks (0=Kick 1=Snare 2=C.Hat 3=O.Hat 4=L.Tom
5=M.Tom 6=H.Tom 7=Clap); 8 sampler slots. Per-step settings: velocity/gate/prob
0..1, ratchet 1..4, tie boolean. `filter.cutoff` is a MIDI note number, not Hz.
The motion sequencer (dialect key `motion`) steps/interpolates the XY Pad's two
assigned params through per-step anchors {step, x, y} in normalized 0..1, plus
two optional single-parameter tracks per bank (motionTracks) that each name
their own parameter id and carry 16 levels. A seqChain slot may also carry a
transpose in semitones (-24..24) — `seqTranspose[]` in the canonical format,
or an `A+5` suffix in the dialect's chain string — so one bank can play a
whole chord progression. It shifts the note the sequencer triggers, never the
stored bank, and only the seq lane has it.

METER (time signature and polyrhythm). A bar is a number of sixteenth-note
ticks, not a fixed 16. Two params in `params` set it: `transport.beats` (2..12)
and `transport.beatUnit` (0 = a quarter is the beat, 1 = an eighth), so a bar is
`beats x (4 or 2)` ticks — 4/4 = 16 (the default, and what every older file
means), 3/4 = 12, 7/8 = 14, 5/4 = 20. Every machine follows it automatically.
Each machine may also override its own loop with `<m>.len` (0 = follow the bar,
else 1..16 cells) and `<m>.rate` (an index into the step-rate list published in
/params.json; the default is one cell per tick, i.e. 1/16), for `m` in
seq/drum/sampler/motion — a lane whose length differs from the bar phases
against it deliberately. The grids stay 16 cells regardless: a shorter lane
simply plays fewer of them, so seqBanks/drumBanks/samplerBanks/motionBanks and
the schemas are unchanged and no song version moved. Note the one limit: a 5/4
or 7/4 bar is 20 or 28 ticks, more cells than a grid has, so those need a
coarser `<m>.rate` (e.g. 1/8 with len 10) to fill a bar.

## Preset formats

A **preset** is a SOUND only — synth parameters, no notes, patterns or tempo.
Two JSON formats are accepted, both imported from the header's Preset button ->
Import (or by pasting them into the app):

- `websynth-preset` (v1) — one sound: `{format, version, name, params}` where
  `params` is a SPARSE map of parameter id -> number. Anything omitted is filled
  from the synth's defaults on import, so an authored preset is always a
  complete, deterministic patch.
  Schema: /schema/websynth-preset.schema.json
- `websynth-preset-bank` (v1) — many sounds in one file, keyed by preset name
  (`presets`). Vintage naming: a preset is one sound, a bank is a collection.
  Schema: /schema/websynth-preset-bank.schema.json

`filter.cutoff` is a MIDI note number here too. Every synth insert effect is
gated by its own `.on` flag. Song-level ids (transport/seq/drum/sampler/arp) are
accepted in a preset but belong in a song.

## The parameter list

Parameter ids, ranges, defaults and discrete value maps are GENERATED from the
running synth's registry — never hand-written, so they cannot go stale — and
published as two files you can fetch directly:

- /params.md   — the prose table, split into sound parameters (what a preset
  carries) and song-only ones. Same lines the in-app prompt shows.
- /params.json — the same list as structured JSON, plus each parameter's
  `taper`, `curve` and `unit`. Shape: `{format: "websynth-params", version,
  songVersion, count, params: [{id, min, max, default, patch, step?, taper?,
  curve?, unit?, labels?}]}`. `patch: true` means the parameter is part of a
  SOUND; `false` means it is song-level (transport, arp, seq, drums, sampler).
  A parameter with `labels` is a CHOICE: its value is the index into that list.

Two other doors serve the same table: the app's Song panel -> "✨ AI Prompt"
(the complete authoring prompt with the PARAMS table inlined), and the MCP
server above (`get_params` for the JSON catalogue, `get_song_format` /
`get_preset_format` for the guides).

## Formats and versions

| Format | Version | Schema | Written by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `websynth-song` | 7 | /schema/websynth-song.schema.json | the app (export) |
| `websynth-song-author` | 1 | /schema/websynth-song-author.schema.json | agents (input only) |
| `websynth-preset` | 1 | /schema/websynth-preset.schema.json | the app + agents |
| `websynth-preset-bank` | 1 | /schema/websynth-preset-bank.schema.json | the app + agents |

Song versioning is ADDITIVE: every bump only adds optional fields, so all
versions 1..7 still load and there is no migration step. Each version added:

- v2 — the sampler fields
- v3 — the XY Pad axis assignment
- v4 — the motion sequencer (XY anchors)
- v5 — `motionTracks` (motion's two extra single-parameter tracks)
- v6 — `seqTracks` (note-sequencer tracks 2-4)
- v7 — `seqTranspose` (a semitone offset per `seqChain` slot)

So a v1 file lacks all of the above; a v6 file lacks only `seqTranspose`. Versions
beyond those a build knows are rejected. The authoring dialect expands to the
LOWEST canonical version that holds its content, not always 7.

## For developers

- The repository's `specs/` folder is the architectural source of truth
  (specs/features/song-authoring-dialect.md documents the author dialect).
- The MCP server for song *and* preset authoring/validation lives in the repo
  under `scripts/mcp/` (see the README). Run locally over stdio it adds two more
  tools, save_song and save_preset, which write importable files; the hosted
  endpoint above omits them because it has no directory a caller can reach.
